security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI (M-mode) or S-mode code uses CSRRS/CSRRC (or CSRRSI/CSRRCI) read-modify-write instructions on pmpaddr CSRs to modify a subset of bits while the CSR is configured in NAPOT mode. During the read phase, the G-1 bit (and possibly other 'reads as' bits) returns 0 instead of its underlying value of 1, and the write-back phase then overwrites those bits with 0, silently corrupting the NAPOT address encoding.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: csr_read_set | csr_read_clear | CSRRS | CSRRC on CSR_PMPADDR with non-x0 rd and non-x0 rs1 while pmpaddr holds NAPOT encoding — any read-modify-write to a subfield of pmpaddr destroys the trailing-ones NAPOT pattern when 'reads as' bits differ from underlying bits
security_spec.summary: CSRRS/CSRRC read-modify-write on pmpaddr CSRs silently corrupts NAPOT 'reads as' bits (e.g., G-1) because the read phase returns the architectural read value (0) rather than the underlying hardware value (1), breaking PMP memory isolation enforced by OpenSBI

findings.finding: pmp_set() uses csr_write_num() (plain csrw) to write pmpaddr CSRs. It computes the NAPOT-encoded address entirely in software and writes it as a full register value. No CSRRS/CSRRC read-modify-write is performed on pmpaddr, so the 'reads as' bits are never read-and-written-back — the NAPOT encoding is never exposed to silent corruption via RMW instructions.

spec_citations.excerpt: When G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg_i.A[1] is set, i.e. the mode is NAPOT, then bits pmpaddr_i[G-2:0] read as all ones. ... Although changing pmpcfg_i.A[1] affects the value read from pmpaddr_i, it does not affect the underlying value stored in that register—in particular, pmpaddr_i[G-1] retains its original value when pmpcfg_i.A is changed from NAPOT to TOR/OFF then back to NAPOT.

findings.finding: pmp_disable() only modifies pmpcfg (clearing the A field to OFF), not pmpaddr. It reads pmpcfg with csr_read_num() (plain csrr) and writes back with csr_write_num() (plain csrw). No CSRRS/CSRRC on pmpaddr at all.

pmp_get() is read-only: it reads both pmpcfg and pmpaddr with csr_read_num() (plain csrr) and does not write back. The NAPOT decoding (ctz(~addr)) correctly handles the 'reads as ones' behavior because when the CSR is read, the hardware returns the 'reads as ones' bits as 1s, which is the correct NAPOT encoding for decoding.

The csr_read_set() macro implements CSRRS (read-modify-write set) and csr_read_clear() implements CSRRC. These macros exist in the codebase but are never invoked on pmpaddr CSRs. Search of all .c/.h/.S files confirms they are only used on MIE, MIP, MSECCFG, MENVCFG, and other non-pmpaddr CSRs.

spec_citations.excerpt: When G ≥ 2 and pmpcfg_i.A[1] is set, i.e. the mode is NAPOT, then bits pmpaddr_i[G-2:0] read as all ones.

findings.finding: Platform cold boot code writes pmpaddr14 and pmpaddr15 with csr_write() (plain csrw). It writes the NAPOT encoding directly (0x1fffffffffffffff for 'all addresses'). No CSRRS/CSRRC on pmpaddr.

Platform cold boot writes pmpaddr13/14/15 with csr_write() (plain csrw). Notably, a FIXME comment at line 382-384 documents that a previous attempt using csr_read(CSR_PMPADDR14) to copy the value failed (system hang), and the code now writes pre-computed constants instead — the correct fix. No CSRRS/CSRRC.

PMP detection writes pmpaddr0 with csr_write_allowed() (plain csrw) to probe PMP address bits, then reads back with csr_read_allowed() (plain csrr). These are single-register write and read operations, not read-modify-write. No CSRRS/CSRRC on pmpaddr.

Smepmp domain configuration calls pmp_set() and pmp_disable() from riscv_asm.c, both of which use plain csrw/csrr on pmpaddr and pmpcfg — never CSRRS/CSRRC. Uses csr_set(CSR_MSECCFG, ...) which is on mseccfg, not pmpaddr.
